results.evidence: In the current snapshot the itinerary days (1,100 + 2,300) do sum to gain_ft 3,400, but that total is impossible for the row's own geography: the approach crosses Early Winters Creek at ~4,080 ft and the summit is 8,507 ft (high_point_ft), and the approach text itself says the bench is ~2,400 ft above the creek, contradicting day 1's 1,100 ft. Sources found only give Burgundy Col approach figures (about 3,500-3,700 ft to the col), not a car-to-car figure for this route, which descends the far side and re-ascends to the col. Settles it: a trip report for the Direct West Face (or a west-face Pernod ascent) stating total gain for the outing.

gain_ft 1,916 is summit minus the 6,100-ft saddle and loss_ft 1,000 is the camp-to-saddle traverse, while the itinerary describes an 8,400-ft trip. A further search found no car-to-car gain or loss for this route alone (only trail-segment figures for Big Beaver and a multi-peak traverse total). Settles it: a single-objective Phantom Peak trip report stating total gain/loss from Hannegan or Ross Lake.

The Pickets overview on one climber's site says access and traversing are easier in early summer and that glaciers open up in August with large crevasses and moats, which supports the chip's late-June start and argues against rating September good. Documented Phantom/Northern Pickets trips found are late June-early July (2016) and late June (2018 traverse); none addresses September on this route. Only one source speaks to the late-season end, so the chip vs September 'good' split stays open; a September ascent report or a second source on late-season conditions for this route would settle it.

results.correct_value: Ice axe and crampons for the Challenger Glacier and steep snow; approach shoes or light boots for the 4th-class sections
results.evidence: The route's approach is the Hannegan / Easy Ridge / Perfect Pass / Challenger Glacier line (FA account). Three independent parties crossing the Challenger Glacier from Perfect Pass carried glacier kit: a July 2020 party used crampons, an ice axe and an ice tool; a July 2021 party used aluminum crampons, ultralight axes and a 30 m rope; an August 2014 soloist used minimal crampons and self-arrested with a tool while threading crevasses. The gear item calling approach shoes or light boots sufficient for the glacier is corrected; rope is already in the list.

patches.expect: Approach shoes or light boots for the glacier/4th-class sections
patches.value: Ice axe and crampons for the Challenger Glacier and steep snow crossings; approach shoes or light boots for the 4th-class sections

results.correct_value: The Big Beaver / Access Creek approach into Luna Cirque is done from late June, with high creek fords and snow in the upper basin
results.evidence: A June 25-27, 2016 party went Big Beaver Trail - Access Creek - Luna Pass and summited Luna Peak, fording Big Beaver Creek at waist height and walking in continuous snow near camp. A separate June 23-24, 2018 party took the same approach and summited, wading streams and finding snow from Luna Col up. Two independent late-June trips show the approach is in usable condition in June, so the itinerary note claiming it is not until mid-July is the outlier; season and guidance (June workable) stand.

patches.find: Northern Pickets approaches are typically not in good condition until mid-July, once Wiley Ridge brush eases and Big Beaver Creek fords back off
patches.replace: Parties reach Luna Cirque from late June, when Big Beaver Creek fords can run waist-deep and snow still covers the upper basin

results.fact: Rock grade of the slab pitches
results.evidence: A retry search found no second description of Phantom Peak's Luna Glacier route; the only route description calls the rock a few leads of class 4 with easy slab climbing and rates the route Easy 5th overall, without saying where the 5th-class move is, and the 5.2-5.4 figures appear in no source. Settles it: a second route description or trip report naming the grade of the slab pitches.

results.fact: Day-1 gain on a 'nearly flat' trail
results.evidence: One account puts the Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp at a gradual thousand feet over about 9 miles and another puts the lakeshore near 1,618 ft, both far below day 1's 1,800 ft. But the itinerary days sum exactly to gain_ft 7,800 (and day 6 loss mirrors it), so correcting day 1 needs a sourced car-to-car total too, which no source states. Settles it: a stated total gain for a Luna Cirque/Phantom outing from Ross Lake.

Both climbing-club route pages put the outing well below 2,150: one states 1,700 ft for the East Ridge, the other gives 1,500 ft trailhead to the Castle-Pinnacle col plus 300 ft to the summit (~1,800 ft). A trip report on the neighbouring scramble route gives ~1,750 ft. The sources still do not agree on one figure, and none states a car-to-car descent for loss_ft. Settles it: a third source stating the East Ridge outing's total gain as 1,700 or 1,800.
